newsitem.title: USA: U.S. attache cuts Mexico corn import estimate.
newsitem.headline: U.S. attache cuts Mexico corn import estimate.

text.p: Mexico's domestic corn consumption will increase slightly over the next year as the economy continues to recover, cutting imports, a U.S. embassy attache said Tuesday.
The Mexico City-based attache said corn imports -- entirely from the United States -- would be 4.2 million tonnes in 1996/97, down from 5.3 million for the previous year.
In a report dated September 18 and released here Tuesday, the attache said the import estimate was down from a previous estimate of 4.5 million tonnes because of the improving Mexican crop.

The corn crop from central Mexico and the state of Chiapas is expected to be good quality. Few problems are expected with aflatoxins in this area because of mild temperatures and normal rainfall, the report said.
